title: Sweetcorn-Crusted Beef and Chicken Bake with Olives and Egg
summary: A Chilean-style baked pie with a thick sweetcorn topping over a spiced beef and shredded chicken filling studded with olives, raisins and egg. The corn crust turns lightly golden in the oven for a comforting, home-style bake.
equipment: large frying pan or sauté pan

ingredients.item: sweetcorn kernels, fresh or frozen and thawed
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blend and cook the corn
steps.text: Blend the corn and milk until mostly smooth but with a little texture left, then tip it into the medium saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring often and scraping the base, until it thickens to a porridge-like consistency. The corn's own starch is what thickens it, so steady stirring stops it catching. Off the heat, stir in the butter, basil and 1/2 tsp salt.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.text: Bring the chicken and water to a bare simmer in the small saucepan, cover and cook gently for 15-20 minutes until the thickest part reaches 74°C on a thermometer. A gentle simmer rather than a hard boil keeps the thighs tender instead of tough. Shred into bite-sized pieces and keep 200 ml of the cooking liquid for the beef.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and starting to turn golden. Cooking them slowly first mellows their sharpness into a sweetness that underpins the whole filling. Stir occasionally so they colour evenly rather than catching in patches.

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.text: Turn the heat up, add the beef mince and cook for 8-10 minutes, breaking it up as you go, until it's cooked through with no raw patches left and a thermometer reads 71°C. Browning it properly before adding liquid builds a deeper, more savoury flavour than simmering it from raw would.

steps.title: Simmer the filling
steps.text: Stir in the cumin, paprika and flour and cook for 1 minute to toast the spices, then pour in the reserved liquid with 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick and juicy rather than wet - the flour binds the liquid into a sauce that won't make the topping soggy.

steps.title: Boil and cool the eggs
steps.text: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until the yolks are fully set, then cool in iced water before peeling and quartering. The quick chill stops further cooking and makes the eggs much easier to peel cleanly.

steps.title: Layer the bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spread the beef filling over the base of the baking dish, scatter over the chicken, egg quarters, olives and raisins, then spread the corn mixture evenly on top and sprinkle with the sugar. The sugar helps the corn crust catch and lightly caramelise as it bakes.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.text: Set the dish on the tray and bake for 30-35 minutes until it's bubbling at the edges and a thermometer in the centre reads 74°C. For a deeper golden top, finish under the grill (broiler) for 2-4 minutes, watching closely so the corn doesn't catch.

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.text: Leave the bake to rest for 10 minutes before serving. This short pause gives the filling a moment to settle so it holds together on the plate instead of spilling out as soon as it's spooned.

tips: Blend the corn only until mostly smooth - a little texture left behind gives the topping a proper, rustic bite rather than a purée.
Don't take the mince off the heat before it's fully browned: any raw patches mean it hasn't reached a safe temperature, so keep breaking it up until it's cooked through.
Taste the beef filling before assembling, since the corn topping on top is only lightly salted.
Measure the sugar sprinkled on top rather than guessing - too much can burn quickly under the grill.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour, then use within 3 days. Reheat a portion in the oven or microwave until piping hot (74°C) and only reheat once. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
